subject: [PATCH v2] mm/hugetlb: allow crashkernel to reuse hugetlb CMA memory

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author disagrees with reviewer's suggestion to separate the patch into multiple commits, considering them too small and simple.
reviews.raw_body:
IMO, the commit and change ins small and simple enough that it doesnt need
to be separated into different commits.

2026-11-10.patch_summary: This patch allows the crashkernel to reuse existing HugeTLB CMA memory when requesting additional memory, rather than reserving dedicated CMA areas only. This is particularly useful on systems that already reserve large amounts of memory with hugetlb_cma=, as it enables the crash kernel to use this existing memory as part of its working set. The patch modifies the architecture code to record the requested CMA size and perform the reservation in mm_core_init_early(), making the HugeTLB CMA areas available for reuse while still allowing memblock to reserve any remainder. This approach ensures that the full HugeTLB CMA pool remains available during normal operation, and after a crash, the capture kernel can use the selected ranges as working memory.
